stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M for co-orbital security
stories.body: True Anomaly secured a $190 million Series C funding, valuing the company at $1.6 billion. The investment underscores the growing demand for co-orbital security and space domain awareness, particularly as the U.S. Department of Defense ramps up its focus on these capabilities. This funding round is a clear sign that investors are betting heavily on the future of space security.
stories.soWhat: In a sector where cash is king, True Anomaly's success reflects a broader trend: defense is where the money is flowing, but can they deliver on the promise?

stories.head: Verde Technologies pivots to space with perovskite panels
stories.body: Verde Technologies is shifting its focus to the space sector, aiming to leverage its perovskite solar panel technology for satellite applications. The move comes as the company looks to capitalize on the growing demand for efficient energy solutions in orbit. This pivot raises questions about whether their technology can perform under the unique conditions of space, which is a bit different from your average rooftop.
stories.soWhat: If Verde can make this work, it could set a new standard for satellite power solutions—if not, they might just find themselves back on the roof.

stories.head: Palantir extends TITAN contract by $480M
stories.body: Palantir Technologies has secured a $480 million extension on its TITAN ground station program, reinforcing its stronghold in government contracts. This extension highlights the importance of familiarity in defense procurement, as agencies often prefer known quantities over new entrants. The deal further cements Palantir's role in the evolving landscape of military tech.
stories.soWhat: In government contracting, being a familiar face can be a golden ticket—Palantir just proved it again.

watchlist.title: Keep an eye on Verde's execution
watchlist.body: As Verde Technologies transitions to space, their ability to deliver will be crucial; failure could set back interest in perovskite tech.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
